title: ComBank pioneers 3DS authentication for UnionPay cardholders - DailyNews
summary:
Commercial Bank of Ceylon, in its commitment to provide secure and world-class technologies to its customers,has further strengthened the security and convenience of online payments for its UnionPay cardholders by becoming the pioneering financial institution in Sri Lanka and the wider South Asian region to introduce advanced 3-D Secure (3DS 2.x) authentication for UnionPay e-commerce transactions.

This milestone makes the UnionPay card a fully empowered e-commerce instrument, enabling cardholders to shop securely at millions of merchants worldwide.

The latest addition to the Bank’s robust 3DS-enabled card portfolio ensures that UnionPay users benefit from the same high-level authentication and fraud protection extended across Commercial Bank’s international card offerings.

The enhancement follows the successful integration of UnionPay cards into the Bank’s ComBank Access Control Server (ACS) platform, enabling secure authentication for online payments through UnionPay’s latest 3-D secure protocol.

Commercial Bank AGM Personal Banking and Retail Products Kapila Liyanage described this latest development as a reflection of the Bank’s commitment to continuously expand Sri Lanka’s digital payment ecosystem. “The benefits of technology must encompass the widest possible customer base to ensure seamless and secure service anywhere in the world,” he said.

UnionPay International, Country Manager – Sri Lanka and the Maldives Crispin Wijesekera said; “The introduction of 3D secure authentication for UnionPay cardholders by Commercial Bank of Ceylon marks an important milestone in strengthening the security and trust of digital payments in Sri Lanka. As e-commerce continues to grow, enhanced authentication technologies such as 3DS provide cardholders with an additional layer of protection while enabling a smooth and convenient online payment experience.”

“UnionPay remains committed to working closely with our banking partners to continuously enhance payment security standards and expand digital acceptance, ensuring that UnionPay cardholders can transact with confidence both locally and globally,” he added.

The new capability introduces UnionPay-specific Risk-Based Authentication (RBA) on the ACS platform. When a customer makes an online purchase at a participating merchant, the system intelligently evaluates the transaction in real time. Where additional verification is required, the system initiates a step-up authentication process by generating a One-Time Password (OTP), which is securely delivered to the cardholder’s registered mobile number and email through the Bank’s established SMS and email gateways.

Where transactions are assessed as low risk, the system allows them to proceed through a seamless ‘frictionless’ authentication flow, enabling fast and convenient payments without additional steps. Together, these capabilities ensure strong protection while maintaining a smooth customer experience for online purchases, the Bank said.

The Bank implemented the new capability by routing the UnionPay 3DS step-up authentication process through its existing OTP distribution infrastructure, allowing seamless integration without requiring complex backend changes.

title: Prime Group wins at Real Estate Asia Awards 2026 - DailyNews
summary:
Prime Group has once again been named Developer of the Year, Sri Lanka at the Real Estate Asia Awards 2026, marking another milestone in a record of consecutive recognition that speaks directly to the confidence placed in the brand.

This achievement comes as Prime Lands Residencies PLC continues to lead Sri Lanka’s condominium sector as the largest real estate entity listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange.

For two consecutive years, Prime Group has been recognised at the Real Estate Asia Awards, reaffirming its continued commitment to excellence, quality, and customer-centric living experiences. This achievement reflects the trust customers place in the company. Each award represents Prime Group’s dedication to delivering homes that go beyond architecture, focusing on lifestyle, comfort, and long-term value.

For customers, this translates into confidence that they are investing in a development that is consistently evaluated and acknowledged at an international level for its standards, reliability, and vision. Prime Lands Residencies PLC operates as the premier condominium development arm of Prime Group, which possesses 30 years of experience in the real estate industry. Throughout its history, the Group has focused on land, housing and condominium developments to shape the national property landscape, establishing a foundation of integrity and customer trust that has stood the test of time.

Winning this recognition for multiple years strengthens what homeowners already experience every day. To date, Prime Lands Residencies PLC has launched over 50 apartment projects across Colombo and its surrounding suburbs, with over 45 of these developments already completed and handed over to homeowners. This consistent delivery demonstrates a reliable performance record and maintains high levels of investor confidence.

“For over 30 years, we’ve built this company on the fundamental belief that a home is defined by more than four walls. These awards validate our customer-centric approach to projects. Being recognised as Developer of the Year at the 2026 Real Estate Asia Awards is not only a testament to the company, but to the thousands of families who placed their confidence in our vision, developments, and long-term value creation. Furthermore, theyreaffirm Prime Lands Residencies’ growth into a destination and investment hub that Sri Lanka now proudly recognizes. This award reaffirms our determination to keep building, not just homes, but trust as well,” said Premalal Brahmanage, Group Chairman of Prime Group.

The company has also introduced innovative payment solutions including the Prime 1% Payment Plan, whilst leading the way with innovative design developments and strengthening its digital footprint through the introduction of the Prime Edge App. Whilst building homes, Prime Lands Residencies remains focused on the creation of thriving communities that provide long-term value for all stakeholders. Prime Lands Residencies PLC continues to reshape skylines and enhance lifestyles through its proven legacy in the real estate sector, remaining committed to raising itsbenchmark year after year.

The Real Estate Asia Awards shine a spotlight on exceptional achievements in the dynamic world of real estate across Asia, recognising those who push the boundaries of innovation and excellence to create lasting impact on their local communities.

title: HNB launches leasing solutions with Hayleys Agriculture to support agricultural growth - DailyNews
summary:
HNB PLC has entered into a strategic partnership with Hayleys Agriculture Holdings Ltd to expand leasing solutions for modern agricultural machinery across Sri Lanka.

Through this partnership, HNB will support farmers and agribusinesses in acquiring tractors, combine harvesters, and other essential agricultural equipment marketed under the globally reputed Kubota and Agrotech brands.

The partnership focuses on improving access to a wide range of agricultural machinery, including the Kubota L4508 Tractor, E-Kubota EK3 471 4WD Tractor, and E-Kubota EK3 501 2WD Tractor under the tractor category. The Combine Harvester range includes the Kubota DC 93G and DC 70G models, alongside the Agrotech 110 Pro. The portfolio is further complemented by machinery such as the Kubota K15 Plus Power Tiller, Agrotech Belt Tractor, and Agrotech Rice Milling Machine.

HNB Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Sanjay Wijemanne stated; “This partnership highlights our long-term commitment to strengthening Sri Lanka’s agricultural community and supporting the wider economy. By improving access to advanced machinery through practical leasing solutions, we are enabling farmers to enhance productivity, strengthen resilience, and invest with confidence.”

This initiative comes at a pivotal time for Sri Lanka’s agricultural sector, where improved efficiency, productivity, and mechanization are essential to supporting national food security and sustainable agricultural development. By combining HNB’s financial expertise with Hayleys Agriculture’s industry leadership, the partnership aims to empower farmers and agribusinesses with access to reliable, advanced, and productivity-enhancing mechanization solutions.

Hayleys Agriculture Holdings Ltd Managing Director Jayanthi Dharmasena said; “Our collaboration with HNB represents a significant step in expanding access to globally recognized agricultural machinery across Sri Lanka. Through the integration of reliable financing and high-quality technology, we aim to empower farmers and agribusinesses with the tools required to enhance efficiency, elevate productivity, and support sustainable growth”.

With its strong legacy in financial services, HNB continues to advance economic progress, while Hayleys Agriculture Holdings Ltd brings deep expertise in delivering innovative agricultural solutions. Together, the two institutions are setting a new benchmark for agricultural financing and mechanization in Sri Lanka.

title: LAUGFS leaders recognised at 45 Under 45 CEO Forum Awards - DailyNews
summary:
LAUGFS Holdings Limited Group Executive Vice Chairman Mithila Wegapitiya and Director/Cluster Chief Executive Officer of LAUGFS Gas PLC, Dr. Niroshan J. Pieries, were recently recognised at the 45 Under 45 Leadership Excellence PlatinumAward organised by the Global CEO Forum, in recognition of their outstanding contribution to leadership, innovation and business excellence.

The internationally recognised awards programme celebrates exceptional business leaders, entrepreneurs, and corporate professionals under the age of 45 who have demonstrated strategic leadership, industry impact and the ability to drive organisational growth and transformation.

The recognition of Wegapitiya and Dr. Pieries reflects LAUGFS Holdings’ continued commitment to cultivating a strong culture of innovation, leadership excellence, and professional growth. As one of Sri Lanka’s leading diversified business conglomerates, LAUGFS remains focused on empowering forward-thinking leaders capable of navigating evolving business landscapes while creating long-term value for stakeholders.

A technology entrepreneur and innovation advocate, Wegapitiya has built a distinguished international career spanning Management & Finance, Global Marketing, Information Technology, and Digital Transformation. Over the past decade, he has worked with globally renowned organisations including Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment, Deutsche Bank, Virtusa Corporation, and Ve Interactive, serving markets across Sri Lanka, the Asia-Pacific region, and the Americas. Widely recognised as a thought leader in emerging technologies, Wegapitiya has actively championed Intelligent Automation, Robotic Process Automation, and Blockchain technologies, driving enterprise digital transformation initiatives across industries. In 2016, he co-founded POTENZA, a global technology consultancy specialising in SAP Consulting, Data and Analytics, and Intelligent Automation, which today operates across eleven countries serving leading regional and global brands.

He currently serves on several industry bodies including the Executive Committee of SLASSCOM’s Intelligent Automation Centre of Excellence and the Board of FITIS, while also being the youngest board member of Sri Lanka CERT|CC, the national organisation responsible for cybersecurity and threat-response coordination.

Dr. Niroshan J.Pieries, meanwhile, brings over two decades of professional experience across sectors including energy, lubricants, logistics, telecommunications, banking, insurance, and customer service. Having held several senior leadership positions within the LAUGFS Group, he has played a pivotal role in driving business transformation, strategic leadership, operational excellence, and brand development across multiple business sectors.

In addition to his corporate responsibilities, Dr. Pieries contributes actively towards academia as a Senior Lecturer in Management and Leadership at several local and international institutions, supporting the development of future business professionals and emerging leaders.

title: George Steuart Insurance Brokers shuffles Board - DailyNews
summary:
In a move aimed at strengthening its corporate structure and long-term plans for the future, George Steuart Insurance Brokers (Pvt) Ltd. (GSIB), a leading corporate insurance and reinsurance broker in Sri Lanka, appointed T. S. Arulanandan (Arul) as its Managing Director and Principal Officer effective from April 1.

Arul counts more than 30 years of management experience in insurance underwriting and brokering. Prior to his appointment as a Director at GSIB, he held the positions of Director-Insurance at Finlay Insurance Brokers (Pvt) Ltd and Managing Director of Finlays Maldives (Pvt) Ltd, in the Republic of Maldives which were subsidiaries of Finlays Colombo PLC.

Arul, an alumnus of INSEAD Singapore/France, brings in a wealth of experience and strength to the GSIB team. He takes over the reins from Joachim Caspersz (Joey) who continues as an Executive Director of the Company. The changes have regulatory approval.

Arul said that he was honoured to be leading GSIB into its next phase of growth. He pointed out that growing the relevance of insurance brokering in Sri Lanka was imperative for the local industry, whilst also stating GSIB’s aspirations of spreading its footprint regionally.

As a broker, GSIB believes it is imperative to embrace innovation and in particular Insurtech solutions for enhanced efficiency benefitting the end customer.

GSIB, he pointed out, was among the first of the local insurance brokers to be specifically licensed to offer reinsurance services and the Company plans on expanding these services. He further said that the company firmly believes that these initiatives will bring in best-in-class value addition to the local industry and its stakeholders.

GSIB has also further strengthened its profile by appointing Ramanan David as Non-Executive Director. Ramanan, who has a wealth of experience in the business andcorporate world, will join alongside the company’s operational directors – Kumar Muthiah, a former Head of Marine at Eagle Insurance under Zurich Sri Lanka and DGM/Head of General Insurance at Aviva/AIA General Sri Lanka, Rohana Weerasinghe heading the claims and technical and Dharini Fernando heading Reinsurance, Cyber Insurance and Specialty Lines.

(GSIB), a leading corporate insurance and reinsurance broker in Sri Lanka, appointed T. S. Arulanandan (Arul) as its Managing Director and Principal Officer effective from April 1.

Arul counts more than 30 years of management experience in insurance underwriting and brokering. Prior to his appointment as a Director at GSIB, he held the positions of Director-Insurance at Finlay Insurance Brokers (Pvt) Ltd and Managing Director of Finlays Maldives (Pvt) Ltd, in the Republic of Maldives which were subsidiaries of Finlays Colombo PLC.

Arul, an alumnus of INSEAD Singapore/France, brings in a wealth of experience and strength to the GSIB team. He takes over the reins from Joachim Caspersz (Joey) who continues as an Executive Director of the Company. The changes have regulatory approval.

Arul said that he was honoured to be leading GSIB into its next phase of growth. He pointed out that growing the relevance of insurance brokering in Sri Lanka was imperative for the local industry, whilst also stating GSIB’s aspirations of spreading its footprint regionally.

As a broker, GSIB believes it is imperative to embrace innovation and in particular Insurtech solutions for enhanced efficiency benefitting the end customer.

GSIB, he pointed out, was among the first of the local insurance brokers to be specifically licensed to offer reinsurance services and the Company plans on expanding these services. He further said that the company firmly believes that these initiatives will bring in best-in-class value addition to the local industry and its stakeholders.

GSIB has also further strengthened its profile by appointing Ramanan David as Non-Executive Director. Ramanan, who has a wealth of experience in the business andcorporate world, will join alongside the company’s operational directors – Kumar Muthiah, a former Head of Marine at Eagle Insurance under Zurich Sri Lanka and DGM/Head of General Insurance at Aviva/AIA General Sri Lanka, Rohana Weerasinghe heading the claims and technical and Dharini Fernando heading Reinsurance, Cyber Insurance and Specialty Lines.

title: DFCC Bank recognised among Lanka’s ‘Top 10 Mom-Inclusive Workplaces’ - DailyNews
summary:
DFCC Bank PLC has been recognised among Sri Lanka’s Top 10 Mom-Inclusive Workplaces at the Mom Leaders Conference 2026, organised by Parenthood Global, highlighting the Bank’s continued focus on creating a workplace where working mothers are supported to grow, lead and succeed.

The recognition reflects DFCC Bank’s efforts to foster an inclusive and supportive workplace culture that enables women to balance professional growth with family responsibilities. It also strengthens the Bank’s positioning as an employer that places people, wellbeing and equal opportunity at the centre of its organisational culture.

As workplaces continue to evolve, support for working parents has become an important measure of inclusive employment. For DFCC Bank, this recognition is linked to the broader environment it continues to build, where employees are encouraged to contribute meaningfully while being supported through different stages of life and career.

DFCC Bank Chief Human Resources Officer Paduma Subasinghe said; “An inclusive workplace is built through consistent action, not only through policy. Supporting working mothers is part of how we create a stronger organisation, because when people are given the space to grow professionally while managing their responsibilities at home, they are able to contribute with greater confidence and purpose. This recognition is meaningful because it reflects the culture we are working to strengthen across the Bank.”

DFCC Bank also celebrated several of its employees who were recognised as inspiring mom leaders at the conference for their dedication, resilience and contribution. They were Nipuni Heiyanthuduwa, Nivirthika Joseph, Venushka Bandaranayake, Sinthuja Sivarajah, Nishadhi Jayasekara, Malindi Dharmawardana, Thilinika Hettiarachchi, Inoka Mutthusamy, Sherine Priyona and Nilushika Chathurangani.

Their recognition reflects the role played by women across DFCC Bank in contributing to the organisation while continuing to manage the demands of family life. It also reinforces the importance of workplaces that recognise talent, commitment and leadership beyond conventional measures of performance.

DFCC Bank’s people strategy continues to focus on building a culture where employees feel valued, supported and empowered to perform at their best. This includes strengthening workplace practices that support inclusion, wellbeing, professional development and equal opportunity.

As Sri Lanka’s development finance pioneer, DFCC Bank continues to build on its institutional legacy by investing not only in customers and communities, but also in its people. The Bank’s recognition among the country’s Top 10 Mom-Inclusive Workplaces marks another step in its journey to create a modern, inclusive and future-ready workplace.

title: People’s Leasing & Finance celebrates 30 years of empowering Lanka’s entrepreneurs and communities - DailyNews
summary:
People’s Leasing & Finance PLC (PLC), one of Sri Lanka’s most trusted Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFIs), celebrates its 30th anniversary on May 31, marking three decades of empowering individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses across the island with innovative financial solutions.

Since its establishment in 1996 as a fully owned subsidiary of People’s Bank, PLC has steadily expanded its footprint across Sri Lanka while strengthening its position as a leading financial service provider of leasing, loans, savings & deposits and other financial services both in conventional and Islamic Financial service.

With an extensive branch network and a dedicated workforce of over 3,000 employees, the company continues to play a significant role in social sustainability supporting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs),focuses on creating long term positive impact on individuals, communities and livelihood who seek reliable financial partnerships to achieve their aspirations.

Over the years, People’s Leasing & Finance PLC has demonstrated resilience and innovation, continuously adapting to the evolving financial landscape. By embracing digital transformation, strengthening operational excellence and maintaining a strong governance framework, the company has successfully enhanced accessibility, efficiency and customer experience across its wide range of financial products and services. This commitment has enabled PLC to remain a trusted financial partner to thousands of customers who rely on its expertise to achieve their personal and business goals.

People’s Leasing & Finance PLC Chairman Prof. Ajantha Samarakoon noted that reaching the 30-year mark is a testament to the unwavering trust and loyalty placed in the company by its customers, employees and stakeholders.

PLC The Sanjeewa Bandaranayake Chief Executive Officer/General Manager also expressed his appreciation to the dedicated employees whose commitment and passion have been instrumental in shaping the company’s success. He highlighted that PLC’s journey over the past three decades has been driven by a strong culture of teamwork, innovation and customer focus. He further emphasized that at People’s Leasing, the company has built long-lasting relationships with its customers by offering financial assistance, guidance and discipline, helping them manage their finances effectively.

To commemorate its 30th anniversary, PLC has planned a series of initiatives throughout the year including media conference, Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) market opening by Bell Ring, Main Anniversary Celebration event with employees at Head office, Launch of 30th Anniversary Commemorative Stamp, Employee Talent Showand impactful corporate social responsibility projects across the island that celebrate the organization’s journey and its contribution to society. These initiatives aim to honor the people, partnerships and communities that have supported PLC’s remarkable growth story.

title: Lanka Hospitals hosts ‘Pulse of Excellence’ awards ceremony - DailyNews
summary:
The Lanka Hospitals Corporation PLC hosted its exclusive ‘Pulse of Excellence’ awards ceremony recently.

The event was organised to recognise and celebrate the institution’s remarkable milestone achievements and outstanding overall performance in 2025.

The ceremony was graced by the Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, Minister of Health and Mass Media and Chief Government Whip, who attended as the Chief Guest and delivered a special address, stating; “These achievements are now an integral part of the hospital’s enduring legacy and a testament to its vital role within our nation’s healthcare sector. Lanka Hospitals has consistently demonstrated that true medical excellence is achieved when world-class clinical standards are driven by a genuine, compassionate duty of care toward the people.”

Other distinguished dignitaries in attendance included Dr. Hansaka Wijayamuni, Deputy Minister of Health and Dr. Priyantha Tennakoon, Director of Private Health Sector Development.

Lanka Hospitals’ continued commitment to shaping the future of healthcare through a comprehensive awards programme, with accolades distributed across several key categories. In the area of Financial and Operational Excellence, departments such as Cardiology, Bariatric Surgery, Neurosciences, Out Patient and Radiology were recognized for record-breaking performances in 2025. Notably, the Neurosciences department was commended for achieving the highest number of advanced neurosurgical procedures during the year.

Furthermore, National and International Excellence Awards were presented to the Departments of Finance, Quality Assurance, Infection Prevention and Control, and Marketing. A significant highlight in this category was the hospital’s prestigious nomination by the World Health Organization (WHO) as the first private mentor hospital for Antimicrobial Stewardship in Sri Lanka.

The ceremony also celebrated leadership and dedication. A highly anticipated Lifetime Service Excellence Award was presented to Mr. Sunil Gamage, Chief Ward Master, in recognition of his enduring commitment and service. Additionally, special recognition was bestowed upon Lanka Hospitals Diagnostics (Pvt) Ltd. in honor of its outstanding service excellence and exceptional financial performance throughout the year.

A major milestone of the evening was the official launch of the LHD Mobile Laboratory Service, which was ceremonially inaugurated during the event.

The gathering was addressed by Lanka Hospitals’ leadership, including Chairman, Maj Gen (Dr) P. A. Chrisaantha Fernando (Retd) and Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Director of Medical Services, Dr. Sanjaya Ratnayake. Emphasizing the collective effort behind the hospital’s success, the Chairman, Maj Gen (Dr) P. A. Chrisaantha Fernando (Retd), stated: “This achievement is never the effort of a single individual or just one department; it is the result of the unity and dedication of our entire staff.”

The evening concluded with the presentation of Privilege Cards to the distinguished guests, followed by a celebratory dinner and fellowship.

title: Sun Siyam Pasikudah brings community together for coastal clean-up - DailyNews
summary:
Sun Siyam Pasikudah, a five-star boutique retreat and part of the Privé Collection within Sun Siyam, reinforced its commitment to community and conservation with a beach cleanup along Pasikudah Bay on May 8.

Held under the group-wide Sun Siyam Cares umbrella, guided by ‘Caring for our People, Nature and Culture’, brought together school students, hotel staff and in-house guests for hands-on environmental action.

Unlike typical cleanup drives, this initiative placed education at its heart. Students from a local school joined guided sessions on coastal ecosystems, the impact of marine litter on biodiversity, and the role every individual plays in protecting Sri Lanka’s coastline, giving young people from the surrounding community a firsthand understanding of why this bay matters, ecologically, culturally, and economically.

Sun Siyam Pasikudah General Manager Arshed Refai said; “What makes this cleanup different is who we did it with. When a child understands why this bay is worth caring for, its ecology, its beauty, what it means to the families who live here, that knowledge stays with them. That is the most sustainable investment we can make.”

Pasikudah Bay’s shallow, crystal-clear turquoise waters and the Eastern Province’s rich marine and cultural heritage, from centuries-old mosques and kovils to the vibrancy of Kattankudy, make it a coastline worth protecting. Participants spread across the shoreline collecting and sorting waste in line with the resort’s zero-waste management principles, while guests noted the activity deepened their connection to the destination beyond a typical resort experience.

Sun Siyam Pasikudah holds the Travelife Gold Certification across 147 criteria spanning energy, water, wildlife, waste, and community welfare. The resort grows over 38 varieties of fruits, vegetables, and herbs on its organic farm, operates solar-powered installations, has eliminated single-use plastics entirely, and sources locally wherever possible. The Sun Siyam Cares Fund supports CarePhant, backing the care of Kalo, a young elephant at the Elephant Transit Home in Udawalawe, ahead of his return to the wild in 2029.

As part of Sun Siyam Resorts, named Most Influential Sustainable Hotel Group of the Year at the 2025 GO TRAVEL Awards, initiatives like this reflect a sustained, year-round commitment to ensuring tourism on the East Coast is a force for renewal, not depletion.

title: Richmond College wins 39th All-Island Inter-School Chemistry Quiz Competition - DailyNews
summary:
Richmond College, Galle emerged victorious at the 39th All-Island Inter-School Chemistry Quiz Competition (ISCQ), organised by the Institute of Chemistry Ceylon (IChemC) in collaboration with the Ministry of Education.

The competition, aimed at enhancing students’ interest in Chemistry and strengthening their understanding of fundamental concepts, was held on May 26, at the newly built IChemC Malabe Campus.

Sixteen schools from across the island were selected for the final stage following a nationwide preliminary round conducted in partnership with the Ministry of Education. Thirteen schools ultimately participated in the final competition.

Based on two written selection tests conducted during the day, four schools qualified for the afternoon oral round. These were Richmond College, Galle; Vembadi Girls’ High School, Jaffna; Seewali Maha Vidyalaya, Ratnapura and Mahamaya Girls’ College, Kandy.

In a closely contested final round, Richmond College secured first place, while Vembadi Girls’ High School claimed second place.

The event was organised by the IChemC Interschool Chemistry Quiz Committee, chaired by Dr. C.N. Ratnaweera University of Ruhuna. The quiz master was Dr. Sashipraba Withanaachchi University of Colombo.

The competition once again highlighted the growing enthusiasm for Chemistry among school students across Sri Lanka and the importance of academic initiatives in nurturing future scientists.

title: Hit-and-run driver remanded till June 16 - DailyNews
summary:
A cab driver involved in the fatal hit-and-run incident that killed six people waiting in a queue at a Vesak dansala in Meegoda has been arrested and remanded until June 16 by the Homagama Magistrate’s Court. The accident occurred on the night of May 31 near Meegoda Junction along the High-Level Road, when a cab travelling from Avissawella towards Colombo veered off the road and ploughed into a crowd gathered at a Vesak dansala.

The vehicle struck the victims before fleeing the scene. Police officers who responded immediately pursued the cab and arrested the driver shortly afterwards.

Reportedly, six people were killed in the crash, including a 15-year-old girl, two women aged 32 and 56, and three men aged 35, 38, and 58. The victims were residents of the Hanwella, Avissawella, and Piliyandala areas. Seven injured victims, including a child, remain under treatment in hospital.

The suspect, a 42-year-old resident of Piliyandala, was found to have been under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident, according to police. He was produced before Court on 10 charges, including culpable homicide, driving under the influence of alcohol, driving without a valid licence, and failing to take measures to prevent the accident. Police further informed the Court that two other individuals were travelling in the cab at the time of the crash. The Magistrate subsequently ordered their arrest and production before Court as investigations by Meegoda Police continue.

Meanwhile, addressing the media, Police said the fatalities could have been prevented had the suspect exercised due care while driving. They warned that motorists who choose to drive under the influence of alcohol and disregard traffic laws will face the full extent of criminal prosecution, including charges that could amount to murder in appropriate cases.

Police further revealed that the driver was intoxicated, did not possess a valid driving licence, and was operating a vehicle with expired documentation.

title: Nineteen motorcycles seized for violating traffic laws - DailyNews
summary:
The Kadawatha Police have seized 19 motorcycles that were being driven loudly and in a manner that was likely to intimidate the public, violating traffic laws, on the night of Vesak Poya day and the following day (30 and 31).

These motorcycles were seized while they were driving on the Colombo-Kandy main road. It is also said that these motorcycles are being ridden in various areas of the Western Province.

A report is scheduled to be submitted to the Mahara Magistrate’s Court in this regard.

After obtaining a report regarding the registration numbers of these vehicles from the Motor Vehicles Commissioner’s Department, charge sheets will also be filed against their owners.

The raid was carried out on the instructions of the Kadawatha Police OIC, Chief Inspector A. D. C. Prasad, along with the Traffic Division OIC, SI Nandana Pathmasiri, Police Sergeants Suraweera, Bandara, PCs Nethmina, Tharaka, Migara, Dinusha, Jayaratne, Nadira and Amarasinghe.

title: Russia says its overnight Ukraine strike was a response to Kyiv's 'terrorist acts' - DailyNews
summary:
Russia says its large-scale overnight missile and drone strikes on Ukraine were carried out in retaliation for what it described as “terrorist acts” by Kyiv against targets inside Russia.

According to the Russian Defence Ministry, high-precision long-range weapons, including hypersonic missiles and drones, were used to target military-related facilities across several Ukrainian regions, including Kyiv, Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities said the attacks killed at least 11 people and injured more than 100 others, with Kyiv among the cities heavily affected.

The strikes come amid escalating tensions between the two countries, with Moscow warning of further retaliatory attacks following recent Ukrainian strikes in Russian-controlled territories. Both Russia and Ukraine continue to deny deliberately targeting civilians. Reuters

title: Trump said to yell at Netanyahu: 'You’d be in prison if not for me’ - DailyNews
summary:
U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly held a tense phone conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, expressing strong opposition to Israel’s recent military escalation in Lebanon.

According to media reports, Trump warned that further attacks, particularly any strike on Beirut, could increase Israel’s international isolation and jeopardise ongoing negotiations between the United States and Iran.

The reports said Trump was concerned that Israel’s actions in Lebanon, including expanded military operations and civilian casualties, could undermine diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing regional tensions.

Following the conversation, Israeli officials indicated that plans to carry out strikes in Beirut had been shelved, although Israel stated it would continue operations against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

title: Domestic dispute leaves six dead in U.S. Iowa shootings - DailyNews
summary:
Six people were killed in a series of shootings in the U.S. state of Iowa on Monday (01), in what authorities believe was a domestic-related incident involving members of the same family.

According to the Muscatine Police Department, the suspected gunman, identified as 52-year-old Ryan Willis McFarland of Muscatine, was also found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Police said officers responding to a shooting report at a residence shortly after noon discovered four people dead from gunshot wounds. The suspect had fled the scene before police arrived.

McFarland was later located on a riverfront trail near a pedestrian bridge with a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Despite receiving medical assistance, he was pronounced dead at the scene.

During the subsequent investigation, detectives discovered the bodies of two additional victims at separate locations, including a residence and a business premises.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the shootings stemmed from a domestic dispute, with all six victims believed to be family members of the suspect.

Authorities have not yet released the identities or ages of the victims. Investigations into the incident are continuing.

title: Indian PM Modi meets Myanmar military gov’t leader in New Delhi - DailyNews
summary:
India says it will continue engaging with Myanmar after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Min Aung Hlaing, the leader of the country’s military government, in New Delhi.

Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri told reporters on Monday that India’s policy is “not intended to be a commentary on the internal political arrangements” in Myanmar and that New Delhi believes engagement is the best way forward.

Western nations have sought to isolate Myanmar’s military rulers since they overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in a 2021 coup that triggered a crackdown on opponents and a brutal civil war.

The conflict began when the country’s army leader, Min Aung Hlaing, ousted the government and detained civilian leaders, including Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

Some critics and human rights groups have said Min Aung Hlaing’s visit to India risks lending legitimacy to the military-backed government.

“We have always proceeded on the principle that sustained dialogue is what is important,” Misri said, adding that isolating Myanmar would be counterproductive.

“History has shown that disengagement doesn’t give us any results that are better than engagement.”

The visit is Min Aung Hlaing’s first to India since he was sworn in as president in April following an election that critics say was designed to cement his hold on power. His last visit to India was in 2019, when he served as Myanmar’s military chief.

He arrived in India on Saturday, first in the eastern state of Bihar, with a visit to the Buddhist pilgrimage site of Bodh Gaya, where believers say that the Buddha attained enlightenment. Al Jazeera

title: Massive overnight Russian strikes hit Ukraine killing at least five - DailyNews
summary:
At least five people have been killed and dozens have been injured after Russia launched a major overnight attack on cities across Ukraine.

Four people were killed in Dnipro and 16 were injured. One person was also killed in Kyiv, where at least 29 were injured following Russian strikes in the early hours of Tuesday.

Thousands of people took shelter in the capital as large plumes of smoke rose from the city’s centre. Air raid warnings were in place across most of Ukraine.

Moscow last week warned it would launch “systematic strikes” on Ukraine in response to a drone strike last month on a dormitory in Ukraine’s Russian-held Luhansk region which killed 21 people.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko has urged people to stay in shelters. The head of Kyiv’s City Military Administration, Tymur Tkachenko, said: “The enemy is striking with ballistic missiles.”

Klitschko said two high-rise apartment buildings had been hit and there are fears people are trapped under rubble.

As the Russian attacks hit Kyiv through the early morning, the buzz of drones could be heard between more than a dozen loud explosions as strikes made impact.

Blackouts and fires have also been reported across the city and the wider extent of damage is not yet clear.

An industrial facility has also been attacked in Zaporizhzhia.

The attacks come after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday reiterated warnings of a possible massive Russian strike and urged residents to pay special attention to air raid alerts.

“Intelligence warnings regarding Russian strikes remain in effect. A massive strike is possible, they have prepared one,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address.

Last week Russia said it would target military and decision-making centres in Kyiv, and urged foreigners to leave the city.

In a statement, the General Staff of Ukraine’s Armed Forces said it did carry out an attack near Starobilsk on the night of 21-22 May, but maintains that it struck a Russian military unit.BBC

title: US and Iran exchange fire as peace deal remains in limbo - DailyNews
summary:
The United States said yesterday (1) that it bombed radar and drone sites in Iran after Tehran shot down one of its drones over the weekend, and Iran then said it launched a strike of its own, in the latest exchange of fire rattling the already fragile truce.

The US military’s Central Command said it carried out the strikes in Iran on Saturday and Sunday around the city of Geruk and on Qeshm Island.

“The measured and deliberate strikes occurred in response to aggressive Iranian actions that included the shootdown of a US MQ-1 drone that was operating over international waters,” Central Command said.

“US fighter aircraft swiftly responded by eliminating Iranian air defences, a ground control station, and two one-way attack drones that posed clear threats to ships transiting regional waters.”

Kuwait said its air defences opened fire early yesterday morning to intercept incoming drones and missiles.

“The General Staff of the Army wishes to advise that any sounds of explosions heard are the result of air defence systems intercepting these hostile attacks,” the Kuwait Army said in a post on its official X account.

Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry later condemned the “heinous and repeated Iranian attacks”.

Around the same time, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said it responded to an American attack without saying where, likely referring to the attack on Kuwait.

In a statement carried by the state-run IRNA news agency, the IRGC said that US forces had targeted a telecommunications tower.

Kuwait is home to US Army Central, its forward command in the Middle East. While the US Air Force no longer flies the MQ-1 Predator, the US Army still does.

Iranian state television later shared footage of the ballistic missile launch, including a close-up showing a sticker on its body depicting a bruised US President Donald Trump overlaid on a “closed” Strait of Hormuz with the caption: “Until the last American soldier leaves the region.”

This is not the first time during the truce that Tehran has targeted Kuwait. Last Thursday, Kuwaiti media reported sirens in the country during the early hours of the morning, after the IRGC claimed it had targeted a US airbase in a missile strike without disclosing its location.

Kuwait also came under repeated fire from Iran during the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Tehran on February 28.

On March 1, an Iranian drone struck a US tactical operations centre at Port Shuaiba, killing six American soldiers and wounding more than 30. Iranian drones also caused significant damage to a government building in Kuwait City on April 5. Kuwait’s commercial aviation has been suspended since the start of the war.

title: Is Russia’s Su-57 Fighter Jet about to become India’s new secret weapon? - DailyNews
summary:
Russia and India are currently engaged in formal consultations regarding the potential local production of the Su-57E, Russia’s fifth-generation stealth fighter, the Russian Federal Service for Military-Technical Cooperation (FSMTC) told Sputnik.. This dialogue follows high-level discussions held during the inaugural International Security Forum in the Moscow Region, where Russian officials reiterated their commitment to expanding bilateral military-industrial cooperation.

The Russian Federal Service for Military-Technical Cooperation (FSMTC) highlighted that these talks are a natural progression of a defence partnership that has thrived for over six decades, during which the two nations successfully established manufacturing pipelines for a wide array of Russian-designed platforms, including Su-30MKI fighter jets, T-90S main battle tanks, and various small arms and ammunition systems.

While Russian aerospace leaders, such as those from the United Aircraft Corporation (UAC), have emphasised the benefits of “licensed production” and the potential to utilise existing Indian infrastructure, such as the facilities currently dedicated to the Su-30MKI, the Indian government remains in the deliberative phase.

Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) leadership has clarified that the project’s future rests entirely with New Delhi’s strategic leadership. Although Russian offers include deep technology transfers and support for India’s domestic Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) program, the Indian Ministry of Defence is carefully weighing these options against long-term sovereignty goals and the need to balance fleet logistics, technical maturity, and self-reliance initiatives like ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’.During the “Wings India 2026” event, Russian aerospace officials, including United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) executives, detailed the proposal for the licensed production of the Su-57E in India. Moscow has consolidated the deal with an offer of full technology transfer, including access to the aircraft’s source code and the localisation of critical components like engines and AESA radar systems.

Russian State arms exporter Rosoboronexport has framed this not just as an export sale, but as a long-term industrial partnership. They suggest that India could utilise existing infrastructure currently reserved for the Su-30MKI fleet to establish a dedicated Su-57E production line, potentially allowing India to bypass years of developmental hurdles. Proponents of the deal argue that the Su-57E could provide the IAF with an immediate, high-performance stealth platform capable of serving as a command-and-control node for drone swarms and network-centric warfare.

title: Rumesh bags Silver at Diamond League - DailyNews
summary:
Champion Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga came up with a brilliant performance to secure second place in the prestigious Diamond League athletics competition held in Rabat, Morocco yesterday. The 23-year-old athlete clinched the second place with a throw of 85.97m on his very first attempt which was his best effort of the night. He also has improved his world ranking with this achievement from 7 to 5 position.

This is the second time a Sri Lankan athlete has participated in a Diamond League tournament and Rumesh created history as the first athlete to represent Sri Lanka in a field event and qualify for a Diamond League.

In this Morocco Diamond League, Rumesh competed with many of the world’s best athletes such as Olympic gold medalist Thomas Röhler, Olympic silver medalist Jakub Vadlejch, World Championship gold medalist Keshorn Walcott, world number 5 Curtis Thompson and world number 6 Julius Yego.

Two time world champion Grenada’s Anderson Peters won the event with a 86.08m throw while former Olympic and World champion Keshorn Walcott of Trinidad and Tobago secured the third place with a 82.52m distance.

Accordingly, the difference between Rumesh and Anderson was a very small figure of 11 centimeters, and Rumesh was able to achieve this victory by defeating all the other world-class champions who participated in the competition. Rumesh’s performance was particularly notable as he outpaced a world-class field of 90m-plus throwers, including Germany’s Thomas Röhler and Kenya’s Julius Yego, who finished fourth and fifth respectively.

Rumesh Tharanga is also scheduled to participate in the next Diamond League tournament to be held in Rome, Italy on June 4 and this first Diamond League achievement gave a big boost to his next games. Rumesh Tharanga is a product of St. Peter’s College Bambalapitiya presently works at Sri Lanka Air Force. His coach Tony Prasanna was also accompanied Rumesh in this meet.

At the 2025 World Championships, Rumesh finished 12th in the qualification round with a throw of 82.80m and became the first-ever Sri Lankan javelin thrower to qualify for the finals, where he placed 7th with a throw of 84.38 m. He is a medal hope at forthcoming Asian Games and Commonwealth Games and also eying for medal in next Olympics in 2028.

Javelin Throw results of the Diamond League Rabat, Morocco:

1. Anderson Peters, (Grenada) 86.08m, 2. Rumesh Tharanga (Sri Lanka) 85.97m, 3. Keshorn Walcott (Trinidad and Tobago) 82.52m, 4. Thomas Röhler (Germany) 81.61m, 5. Julius Yego (Kenya) 80.59, 6. Curtis Thompson (United States) 77.88m, 7. Jakub Vadlejch (Czechia) 77.75m, 8. Dawid Wegner (Poland) 71.18m.

title: Kohli inspires RCB to back-to-back IPL titles - DailyNews
summary:
The IPL 2026 season came to a memorable end with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) successfully defending their title and becoming only the third franchise in tournament history to win back-to-back championships. After ending their long wait for a maiden trophy in 2025, RCB followed it up with another dominant campaign, defeating Gujarat Titans in the final in Ahmedabad on Sunday.

While RCB celebrated team success, the season also belonged to Rajasthan Royals’ sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who emerged as the biggest individual star of the tournament. The 15-year-old swept multiple awards, including the Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Fantasy Player of the Season, Super Striker of the Season, and Super Sixes of the Season, underlining his extraordinary impact with the bat.

RCB restricted Gujarat to 155-8, a total they chased down with 12 balls to spare after Virat Kohli reached his fifth half-century of the season (unbeaten 75 ) in a largely one-sided final in Ahmedabad. Kohli sealed the win in style – striking the winning runs with a six to cap a magnificent 42-ball innings featuring nine fours and three sixes.

Rajasthan Royal opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi receiving the Emerging Player award

Kohli said RCB were the “best team in the comp” and praised a “clinical performance” by his team-mates as they secured their second IPL title having won it for the first time in 18 years in 2025.

RCB’s seamers set up the victory as Rasikh Salam Dar stood out with 3-27 in a disciplined attack alongside experienced campaigners Josh Hazlewood and Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who both took two wickets each.

Only Washington Sundar offered much resistance as he scored a defiant 50 not out while England’s Jos Buttler was stumped for 19.With the stadium awash with shirts bearing Kohli’s name and iconic number 18, the former India captain delivered once again on the biggest stage.

Mohammed Siraj made the breakthrough by dismissing Iyer, before Kagiso Rabada removed Devdutt Padikkal to give Gujarat with an opening. Rashid Khan then swung momentum further in the Titans’ favour, claiming two wickets in an over as captain Rajat Patidar fell for 15 and Krunal Pandya followed soon after. But Kohli, who retired from T20 internationals after the 2024 World Cup, remained stoic, as he shared a crucial 41-run partnership with Tim David to steady the chase. David made 24 before departing, which left Kohli to guide RCB home alongside Jitesh Sharma. Kohli even provided the iconic ending the majority of those inside the stadium craved as he crashed Arshad Khan over long-on for six to seal the victory. Kohli won the player-of-the-match award.

The 15 year old Rajasthan Royal opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, was adjudged most valuable player of IPL and Emerging Player of the Season while he also won the Orange Cap for being the highest run-getter (776) . The teenager also won the award for hitting the most sixes (72) as well as the Super Striker award (for the highest strike rate of 237), and won a Tata Sierra Car. The Gujarat Titans paceman Kagiso Rabada won the Purple Cap for being the highest wicket-taker (29 wickets) Gujarat Titans opener Sai Sudharsan won the award for the most fours (75). KKR’s Manish Pandey won the award for the Catch of the Season for taking Tim David’s catch at backward point while Gajrat Titans paceman Mohammed Siraj won an award for bowling the most dots (172). Fairplay award was won by PunjabKings. The champion RCB team won Indian rupees 20 core while runners up Gujarat Titans won 12.5 rupees Indian core. (Agencies)

Gujarat Titans 155 for 8 wickets in 20 overs (Washington Sundar 50*,Nishanth Sindhu 20, Rasikh Salam 3/27, Buwaneshwar Kumar 2/29)

Royal Challengers Bengalalu 161 for 5 wickets in 18 overs (Virat Kholi 75*, Venkatesh Iyer 32, Rashid Khan 2/25, Arshad Khan 1/32)

title: Sri Lanka shine at Asian Junior Squash C’ships - DailyNews
summary:
Sri Lanka’s young squash players delivered a series of notable performances at the 33rd Asian Junior Individual Squash Championships held in Panzhihua, China, winning three Plate titles and several top placements against the best junior players in Asia.

Leading the boys’ performances, Royal College player Manuth Dasanayake emerged as the Under-17 Boys Plate Champion after an outstanding campaign. Fellow Royal College player Tarul Pinwattha finished as the Under-19 Boys Plate runner-up, while another Royalist, Nevan Rubasinghe, claimed the Under-15 Boys Plate runner-up position.

In the girls’ category, Ladies’ College star Nethmi Wickramasinghe captured the Under-19 Girls Plate Championship to give Sri Lanka its first girls’ Plate title. Sirimavo Bandaranaike Vidyalaya’s Thedara Liyana finished as the Under-17 Girls Plate runner-up, while Gateway College player Chanumi Thebuwana added another title by winning the Under-15 Girls Plate Championship.

Sri Lanka also achieved encouraging results in the Main Draw competition. Gateway College’s Sithumuli Mendis finished 11th in Asia in the Under-17 Girls category, underlining her ability to compete among the continent’s leading juniors.

Meanwhile, Ladies’ College youngster Sayuri de Silva secured 13th place in Asia in the Under-13 Girls category. Her performance has marked her out as one of Sri Lanka’s most promising young squash players and a bright prospect for the future.

In the Girls’ Under-15 division, Methuki Herath, Navya Ganegoda, and Dinithma Mihely also performed strongly in the Super Plate round, securing commendable positions and showcasing Sri Lanka’s growing depth of talent at the junior level.

Beyond the players, Sri Lanka was proudly represented among the tournament officials. World Squash Officiating (WSO) referees Sasindu Thrimavithana and Priyantha Ishara served on the international refereeing panel, reflecting the growing recognition of Sri Lankan officials on the Asian stage.

The team was supported by a highly qualified coaching staff comprising World Squash Federation-certified coaches Chaminda Thalagala, Mahesh Chandana, Thushara Wasantha Kumara, and Ashan De Silva, who provided technical expertise and guidance throughout the championship.

The administrative delegation was led by Team Managers Wing Commander Sanjeewa Nanayakkara, Assistant Secretary of Sri Lanka Squash and Wing Commander Lahiru Abeyrathne, Tournament Director of Sri Lanka Squash.

title: Sri Lanka team to Asian Rowing Beach Sprint C’ships - DailyNews
summary:
Sri Lanka’s Beach Sprint Rowing team departed for Thailand to participate in the prestigious Asian Rowing Beach Sprint Championships 2026 and the Youth Athlete Development Training Camp, marking another important milestone in the country’s growing presence in international coastal rowing.

The team will first participate in the Youth Athlete Development Training Camp followed by the Asian Rowing Beach Sprint Championships from June 4 to 7 at Jomtien Beach, Pattaya, Chonburi, Thailand. The Sri Lankan delegation comprises four members, including three athletes and one coach.

Sri Lankan Team: Major Maheshi Liyanage – Senior Women’s Single Scull (CW1x), Denver Deheragoda – Under-19 Men’s Single Scull (CM1x) and Mixed Double Scull (CMix2x), Vethmi Weeraratne – Under-19 Women’s Single Scull (CW1x) and Mixed Double Scull (CMix2x), Mangala Alagiyawanna – Coach.

The tour carries special significance for Sri Lankan rowing as Major Maheshi Liyanage becomes the first female athlete to represent Sri Lanka at an international Beach Rowing Championship in the Senior Women’s category.

Meanwhile, young rower Vethmi Weeraratne creates history as the first athlete from Visakha Vidyalaya, Colombo to represent Sri Lanka at an international rowing championship.

The team is expected to compete against leading Asian rowing nations in the rapidly developing discipline of Beach Sprint Rowing, a dynamic format that combines beach running, open-water rowing, buoy turns, and sprint racing.

Participation of the Sri Lankan team at this championship will provide valuable international exposure and will contribute significantly toward the future development of coastal rowing and beach sprint rowing in Sri Lanka. The championship is organised by the Rowing and Canoeing Association of Thailand (RCAT) under Asian rowing competition regulations.

title: Kiwi expert Woods rejoins Sri Lanka Sevens setup - DailyNews
summary:
Sri Lanka Rugby has appointed experienced New Zealand coach Peter Woods as the new Head Coach of the Sri Lanka Men’s Sevens Rugby Team, with the national outfit preparing up for a busy international season that includes the Asian Sevens Series and the Asian Games.

Woods is no stranger to Sri Lankan rugby, having previously guided the Tuskers Sevens team from 2016 to 2018. During his earlier stint, he led the side through major international competitions including the Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games.

The former New Zealand representative player returns with a wealth of coaching experience and a strong reputation for developing young talent. He has played a key role in nurturing players through New Zealand’s highly competitive Bay of Plenty Sevens programme, one of the country’s leading rugby development pathways. Sri Lanka Rugby believes Woods’ experience and knowledge of the local rugby environment will be a valuable asset as the national team seeks to strengthen its position in Asian rugby.

The official contract signing ceremony is scheduled to take place in Colombo today, June 2.

Woods’ immediate focus will be preparing the Sri Lanka Men’s Sevens squad for the Asian Sevens Series, which will be held in Sri Lanka and China later this year, before turning attention to the Asian Games in Japan.

title: Hope carries Windies’ hopes against SL in June - DailyNews
summary:
West Indies have announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming ODI series against Sri Lanka, with Shai Hope set to captain the side. The squad sees the return of Left-handed batter Shimron Hetmyer and fast-bowler Alzarri Joseph. Hetmyer, who has been reintegrated into the ODI setup as part of Cricket West Indies strategic build-up towards the 2027 ICC Men’s ODI World Cup, will join the squad ahead of the third and final match of the series. Joseph, the right-arm quick has been out of action since July 2025 due to a back injury and is in line to play his first international cricket since Australia toured the Caribbean last year. Spinner Gudakesh Motie, who missed the tour of New Zealand in November, also finds his way back into the squad.

The ODI squad comprises Shai Hope (captain), Akeem Auguste, John Campbell, Keacy Carty, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Justin Greaves, Shimron Hetmyer, Amir Jangoo, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Sherfane Rutherford, Jayden Seales and Shamar Springer.

West Indies squad arrived in Jamaica on May 31 following the conclusion of the 10-day training camp at the Coolidge Cricket Ground in Antigua.

The three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka will be played at Sabina Park in Jamaica on June 3, 6 and 8. The three-match T20I series will play from June 11 to 14, followed by a two-match Test series in Antigua from June 25 to July 7. Lankan ODI team led by Kusal Mendis already in Jamaica while Eshan Malinga and Dilshan Madushanka both have been involved in IPL left yesterday to join the team.

title: Eshan most successful Lankan bowler at IPL - DailyNews
summary:
Sri Lankan right arm fast bowler Eshan Malinga had a successful IPL capturing 20 wickets in 15 matches with best figures of 4 for 32.

The 25 year old Eshan played for Sunrises Hyderabad for the second time in a row and was praised by skipper of Sunrises Hyderabad Pat Cummins. His ability to bow at death overs always gave success to Hyderabad team before losing to Gujarat Titans the IPL runners up this time. As soon as he finished his IPL duty Eshan Malinga returned home and left for West Indies yesterday to join the Sri Lanka team .Eshan and Dilshan Madushanka both were in same Hyderabad team while Sri Lanka legends Muttiach Muralitharan and trainer Mario Villawarayan were also among the Sunrises Hyderabad supporting staff.

Eshan Malinga in action at IPL

Eshan Malinga came on a difficult journey . He hails from Opanayake in Ratnapura and lacked facilities Eshan .studied at Ratnapura Seewali College and he is the first player to represent National team from his school . I didn’t play hardball cricket until I was 18 years old. The big match was my first hardball match. I won the man of the match award. After that, people started calling me Opanayake Express.. However with the limited facilities I decided to stop playing cricket because I wanted to take care of my family. We are not rich. My father is a driver. But my family told me not to give up. If you want to do something, you have to sacrifice a lot. I did that. and I am very happy to come on this journey said Eshan.

In 2025, Eshan followed a seven-game IPL stint (13 wickets) for Sunrises Hyderabad with his T20I debut for Sri Lanka later in the year, and gained valuable experience. Before I played IPL, I didn’t play many T20 matches. Just one LPL and eight domestic T20 games. I didn’t have a lot of experience. Playing in the IPL gave me that strong mindset said Eshan Malinga.

As a fast bowler, I think my biggest strength is the yorker, and reverse swing and the slow ball bouncer. I have a few variations . That’s my strength added Eshan Malinga .

“Everyone [in the IPL] is coming out to hit and we as bowlers too want to go hard against them. But sometimes we have to go with a defensive mindset.

Learning those things helped me when I joined the national side. It helped me on how to handle a situation and make decision-making. Eshan Malinga remembered his journey from Ratnapura to Colombo .

Back home in Ratnapura, a young Eshan would tie clothes between two trees at his home and keep bowling at it.The fast bowling coach Chamila Gamage found his action repeatable and pace was impressive even then, and gladly enrolled him at his training academy a few years later for him to play leather ball cricket.

When I was in Ratnapura I had chance to take part in Airtel Fast bowling programme at Badulla and I bowled at 127 kmph speed on that occasion. I was selected for Colombo programme with my achievements and that was the turning point of my career said Eshan. The best 50 players were in this training camp handled by legends Chaminda Vaas, Hashan Thilekeratne , Anusha Samarahayake who gave their support and I had chance to bowl on turf wickets for the first time . I applied for this programme at my Mothers request.

At Colombo programme I bowled at 131 kmph speed and finally at the final training programme I bowled 141 kmph speed and got a real boost.

The fast bowling coach Chamila Gamage always worked with me to develop my skills and even today Eshan contacts fast bowling coach Chamila to get his advice. Chamila Gamage the fast bowling coach said Eshan always has good commitment during practices and his dedication helped to get success . Unfortunately he couldn’t take part in last T-20 world cup due to injury and that was a big loss for the Sri Lanka team . Getting IPL for the second time gave big boost to develop his career said Chamila Gamage. His slinging bowling action is always a big challenge for opponent batters said Gamage .

Gamage introduced Eshan to step-bowling. In the nets under Gamage’s supervision, Eshan would bowl 20-30 deliveries from just a single step run-up. Then he would graduate to two steps, and then three and four before finally moving on to the full run-up. “Sometimes he would bowl only three or four steps all day. This helps in understanding how he’s feeling physically, how he’s releasing the ball and visualizing his ideas,” Gamage explains. For swing, they’d condition his wrists by training with a heavy ball for hours .

Eshan arrived in India for IPL 2026 with a targets in mind: to pick 20 wickets and he did it with more determination. He should have get more wickets but unfortunately few catches were dropped off his bowling and that’s cricket and we cannot control those said Chamila However

I am sure his performance for National team against West Indies will be more successful for the Sri Lanka team .

title: Sri Lanka ruggerites stun French rivals to bag Shield Title - DailyNews
summary:
Sri Lanka’s historic Shield Championship victory at the Howard Hinton Sevens tournament in France is far more than a trophy-winning performance. The Tuskers’ dramatic 28 points (four goals) to 21 (three goals) comeback win over French side Pyla Sevens Rugby after trailing 7-21 at half-time has sent a strong message that Sri Lankan rugby can compete with physically stronger and more experienced European teams.

For many years, Sri Lankan rugby has searched for opportunities to test itself against higher-level opposition outside Asia. The Howard Hinton Sevens provided exactly that platform. Playing against European club teams known for their physicality, speed and sevens experience, the Tuskers were pushed to their limits throughout the tournament.

What made the final victory even more impressive was the manner in which it was achieved.

At half-time against Pyla Sevens Rugby, Sri Lanka appeared to be heading towards defeat. The French outfit dominated the opening period and established a convincing 21-7 lead. Sri Lanka’s only response came through winger Gayan Perera, who crossed for a crucial try that kept his side within touching distance.

However, the second half revealed a different Sri Lankan team. Instead of surrendering to the pressure, the Tuskers displayed fighting spirit and belief. Diluksha Dange and Janidu Dilshan crossed the line as Sri Lanka gradually clawed its way back into the contest. Their efforts levelled the scores at 21-all and shifted the momentum firmly towards the Asian side.

With the final seconds ticking away, Suranga Tennakoon produced the decisive moment of the match. His last-minute try completed one of Sri Lanka’s finest comeback victories in recent sevens rugby and secured a memorable Shield Championship triumph.

The victory highlighted an important characteristic that has often defined successful Sri Lankan teams — the refusal to give up when faced with adversity.

Head Coach Shamlie Nawaz, speaking from France after the victory, praised his players’ fighting spirit.

“Sri Lanka won the match in the last minute without giving up until the very last second. The players understood the physical challenge and adjusted themselves during the game,” Nawaz said.

“They also understood the level of competition in European sevens rugby. That experience is extremely valuable for our players.” The coach noted that the team had to overcome several difficulties during the tour.

“We had hardships throughout the tournament. Two sevens players, Dinal Ekanayake and Shahid Zumri, were unavailable due to injuries sustained while playing club fifteens rugby. Despite those setbacks, the players kept fighting and believed until the final minute,” he said.

The final was not the only impressive performance from the Tuskers. Earlier, Sri Lanka defeated Euskadi 22-15 in the Shield semi-final after taking a commanding 17-5 lead at the break. The victory demonstrated the team’s ability to control matches from the outset while also showing the composure needed to withstand a late challenge.

Even before that, Sri Lanka had displayed remarkable character against Mauritius in the Bowl qualification match. Trailing 0-17 at half-time, the Tuskers mounted a spirited comeback to level the scores at 19-all. Although Mauritius eventually escaped with a narrow 24-19 victory, the fightback hinted at the resilience that would later help Sri Lanka capture the Shield title.

Captain Srinath Sooriyabandara led the side admirably throughout the tournament, while Akash Madushanka, Gayan Perera, Diluksha Dange, Janidu Dilshan, Suranga Tennakoon and Chathura Soysa played vital roles in Sri Lanka’s successful campaign.

Beyond the results, the tour exposed Sri Lankan players to a style of rugby rarely experienced at home. European sevens rugby places a heavy emphasis on physical strength, speed at the breakdown and decision-making under pressure. Competing against such opposition provides lessons that cannot be replicated in domestic competition.

Nawaz also acknowledged the support received from the Sri Lanka Rugby administration in making the tour possible. “I am very happy with the support given by the current Sri Lanka Rugby President. He worked hard to find sponsors and create opportunities for international exposure. These tours are very important for the future of Sri Lankan rugby,” he said.

Nawaz also acknowledged the support received from the Sri Lanka Rugby administration in making the tour possible. “I am very happy with the support given by the current Sri Lanka Rugby President. He worked hard to find sponsors and create opportunities for international exposure. These tours are very important for the future of Sri Lankan rugby,” he said.

title: Double delight for Dinara in final ITF junior appearance - DailyNews
summary:
Sri Lanka’s number one tennis player, Dinara de Silva, brought the curtain down on her International Tennis Federation (ITF) junior career in perfect fashion by capturing both the girls’ singles and doubles titles at the SSC-ITF International Junior J30 Tournament Week One at the SSC Courts in Colombo, delivering a memorable farewell on home soil.

Ashlin de Silva (left) and Mayooran Kubherane pose with the boys’ doubles runners-up trophy at the SSC-ITF International Junior J30 Tournament in Colombo.

The talented St Bridget’s Convent player showed her class and composure throughout the tournament and saved her best for last. In her final ITF junior appearance, Dinara defeated Hong Kong’s Hiu Lam Ella Wong 7-6, 6-4 in a hard-fought girls’ singles final to lift the championship trophy. The victory marked a fitting end to a successful junior career that has seen her become one of Sri Lanka’s brightest tennis prospects.

Dinara’s route to the title was equally impressive. In the semi-finals, she produced a dominant display to crush India’s Ahida Sing 6-0, 6-0, underlining the gap between herself and the rest of the field.

The tournament also highlighted the growing strength of Sri Lankan women’s tennis. Youngster Yuhansa Peiris enjoyed an excellent run before her campaign ended in the semi-finals. She fought bravely against eventual runner-up Hiu Lam Ella Wong of Hong Kong but went down 6-3, 3-6, 10-3 in a closely contested encounter.

Dinara was not finished with her winning ways. Teaming up with fellow Sri Lankan Yuhansa Peiris of Bishop’s College, she secured a second title by winning the girls’ doubles championship. The Sri Lankan pair defeated Hong Kong’s Ling Sum Kanna and Hiu Lam Ella Wong 5-4, 5-4 in the final, completing a memorable double triumph for the host nation.

In the boys’ doubles final, Sri Lanka’s Ashlin de Silva and Mayooran Kubherane of St Peter’s College came close to claiming the title but were narrowly beaten by India’s Fazal Ali Meer and Singapore’s Zachary Sag. The Sri Lankan pair lost 5-4, 3-5, 10-8 after a thrilling contest that went down to the wire.

title: Royal divers take Novices Championship - DailyNews
summary:
Royal College emerged as the overall boys’ champions with 98 points at the 18th Sri Lanka Novices Diving Championships 2026, sponsored by MILO and held at the Sugathadasa Aquatic Sports Complex in Colombo recently.

Guided by coach Chanaka Wickramasinghe and led by captain Yusuf Shihar, Royal produced a commanding display across the younger age groups to finish ahead of St. Benedict’s College (51 points) and St. Joseph’s College (49 points).

In the oldest age category contested, the Under-20 division, St. Benedict’s College diver Thenuka D. Unagolla won the 1m springboard title with 85.55 points. His teammate John Keil finished second with 80.10 points while Sheran Premathilaka of St. Joseph’s College claimed third place with 64.25 points. Royal College divers Sandun Siriwardana and Kishan Praveen finished fourth and fifth respectively.

In the Under-20 3m springboard event, Sheran Premathilaka of St. Joseph’s College secured the title with 59.10 points. John Keil of St. Benedict’s College was second with 55.65 points while Royal College’s Kishan Praveen took third place with 50.20 points.

The Under-16 category produced a close battle in the 1m springboard event where Diyan Shenal of St. Joseph’s College won with 80.55 points. Oshanda E. Perera of St. Benedict’s College was a close second with 79.80 points while Muhammed Maznavi of Royal College finished third with 64.40 points.

Oshanda E. Perera turned the tables in the Under-16 3m springboard event, claiming first place with an impressive 95.95 points. Diyan Shenal finished second with 63.30 points.

The Under-14 events saw strong competition among several schools. In the 1m springboard contest, Maheesha Eshan of St. Joseph’s College captured the title with 76.70 points. M.K. Thinuga Damsara of Thurstan College finished second with 75.80 points while Lahan De Silva of S. Thomas’ College was third with 74.05 points. Sasru Nethush and A.S. Rayan of St. Benedict’s College, along with D.H. Risara Prabashwara of Thurstan College, also featured prominently.

In the Under-14 3m springboard competition, Sasru Nethusha of St. Benedict’s College secured first place with 62.35 points. Maheesha Eshan of St. Joseph’s College finished second with 60.80 points while Lahan De Silva of St. Thomas’ College claimed third place with 57.50 points.

Royal College dominated the Under-12 category. In the 1m springboard event, Asel Lakviru won the title with 119.45 points ahead of teammates Manuth Kulappuarachchi (94.95) and Sehas Wijesundara (84.80). Radith Suraweera, Rajindh Kirindomana and Senuja Rajapaksha completed another strong showing for Royal.

The same school continued its dominance in the Under-12 3m springboard competition. Asel Lakviru secured another gold medal with 116.50 points while Sehas Wijesundara and Manuth Kulappuarachchi finished second and third respectively. Senuja Rajapaksha, Radith Suraweera and Rajindh Kirindamane added further depth to Royal’s challenge.

The Under-10 category belonged entirely to Royal College. Keshawa Devendra produced an outstanding performance to win both the 1m and 3m springboard titles with scores of 111.95 and 110.45 points respectively. Teammate Vinuth Kulappuarachchi finished second in both events while Laaiq Ulfath claimed third place in the 1m competition and Vishwa secured third place in the 3m event.
